findings.summary: the preferred-article rule is only half driven by this walk
findings.detail: This step proves an INCOMPLETE article does not cost. It does not prove the harder half of `MarginPriceResolver`: that an incomplete PREFERRED article suppresses a COMPLETE rival, so an ingredient with two perfectly good priced suppliers resolves to no price at all. `utils/margin/supplier-model.js` calls that the case the file exists for, and `mrg_item_preferred_blocks` — which this walk does render — is the venue-facing warning for it. Driving it needs a second supplier selling the same ingredient; no journey in this repo builds one, so nothing here is evidence for that branch.

findings.summary: the dark module refuses its own status read; the fixture does not
findings.detail: On the live backend the pre-lever visit to /admin/margin-suppliers was answered 404 `margin.not-found` on GET /margin/status (1 time(s)) — the module-invisible refusal MarginStatusController documents as MARG-L10 — and the page rendered the module-off blocker from that coded 404. The fixture serves /margin/status unconditionally (200 with flags.module:false), so this walk’s fixture captures all show zero refused requests where a real venue’s browser records one. The page handles both shapes; the fixture hid the refusal, not a defect.
